BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's assertion that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the disclosure/limitation package is "already accepted" is a counterparty assertion, not a Wattlebridge instruction. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 nothing is cleared until confirmed through our own authority process. No such confirmation exists on the file (no Amelia Frost written authority for any fallback). I have therefore reviewed **every** clause on its merits and treated the [STANDARD] tags as having no effect.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our fallback number only coincidentally – the fallback requires prior written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure converts the basket into a further AUD 250,000 cap reduction.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months.
- Recommendation: **Reject; hold at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval, which has not been given; a number matching a fallback does not clear it.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Folding title and capacity into a 20%/18-month regime leaves the Buyer with no meaningful recourse if it does not actually own the shares it paid AUD 24m for.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: none offered; cl 12.3 ("limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated") and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature") would sweep fraud into the caps, time limits and non-reliance.
- Buyer wants: express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "all Claims of any nature" wording and insert an express fraud carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook position and the Seller's drafting is a direct (if implicit) attempt to limit it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DL 1.1, DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2), plus a blanket non-admission (DL 1.4).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure rejected.
- Recommendation: **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2; require a fair-disclosure standard with specific disclosures only.** Whole-data-room disclosure would effectively qualify every warranty by documents the Buyer may not have been able to identify as relevant.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: blanket exclusion deleted; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, mirrored by named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard is a constructive-knowledge bar that duplicates the whole-data-room disclosure and would gut the warranty package.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours only; consent deemed satisfied on mere delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions is in the data room.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent requiring effective Bluefen consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; re-draft as a hard CP with conditions-satisfied evidence.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery give no protection if the consent is conditional and the conditions fail.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost approval – neither is in place, and a debt-free/cash-free deal cannot close with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller (or deducted from price); no silent exclusion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require itemisation and seller funding, including on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) bears the liability by default.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering non-transfer/defective title in the SOW3 Project Materials, any Ironquay claims and consequential loss, while preserving the cure (pay outstanding fees and obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion).
- Recommendation: **Reject as inadequate; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion cure or evidence.** The exposure is loss of IP ownership, not just an AUD 180,000 payment – and that figure is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL para 6: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification status not established; no breach characterisation; no loss amount.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, a completed investigation, written updates through to Completion, a specific warranty on the facts, and a specific indemnity for any resulting notification costs, regulatory action or claims.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; impose preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** We should assume neither a confirmed breach nor the absence of one – the point is to allocate the unknown risk to the Seller, not to quantify it now.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8: DD-008/DD-011 silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: factual assessment of timing, scope and terminability before classification; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Reserve position; request the renewal terms and payment status, then classify.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but the playbook does not support a reflexive price deduction either.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: all limitations apply to "all Claims" unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3); limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each on their own regime, with no hidden general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject the catch-all wording and insert an express priority clause.** The "all Claims" drafting is the mechanism by which the Seller collapses Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into a 20%/18-month cap.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL para 10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC searches, PPSR searches, constitution, board/shareholder authorisations, share certificates, encumbrance confirmations and Riverlark security release.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as proof of title; commission independent searches and make them a Completion deliverable.** A seller-supplied internal register is the thing being verified, not the verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considers tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN, negotiated separately with their own cap, period and basket treatment (the playbook does not assume unlimited liability, nor any agreed resolution).
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" assertion and mark Tax/IP as OPEN in the issues list.** Nothing on our side has agreed these terms; the Seller's statement is an attempt to close an open point by assertion.

---

**Overall:** Of the sixteen issues, none is acceptable as drafted; thirteen require outright rejection and counter-proposals, two (Sandbar, Export incident) require fact-gathering before a final position, and one (Tax/IP) must simply be re-opened. No fallback positions should be deployed in the mark-up until written authority from Amelia Frost is obtained and recorded against this specific draft. I recommend the response to Seller's counsel open by expressly rejecting the "pre-categorised / already accepted" framing so it cannot later be cited as an agreed basis for negotiation.
